propositions: The byte-total backstop trigger promised in ADR 0005 and the janitor module contract is unimplemented; _gc_pass reads only free-space and mtime, never consulting _cache.byte_total, leaving no size-based reclaim mechanism
materialize_tickets bypasses cache.acquire entirely and never calls add_bytes, causing ~620 MiB ticket entries to be invisible to the incrementally-maintained byte-accounting counter
No configurable store-size cap knob exists in the config surface (REBAR_GATE_MAX_BYTES, [snapshot] max_bytes, or defaults)
The dominant entry class (tickets-<sha>, ~861 MiB each) contributes zero to byte_total accounting while startup_sweep's reconciliation walk counts them, creating divergence
Two independent gaps combine to leave the snapshot store with no functional size-driven reclaim: the backstop unimplemented and the largest consumer unaccounted
